references.text: The preceding verse tells of the flight of the five kings and that they hid in the cave at Makkedah, which leads directly to the message Joshua receives.
These verses describe what happened to the five kings after they were found in the cave—they were executed and hung on trees, then placed back in the cave.
Here the five kings are named by name—Adoni-Zedek of Jerusalem, Hoham of Hebron, Piram of Jarmuth, Japhia of Lachish, and Debir of Eglon—who are the same kings found in the cave.
Rahab advised the spies to hide in the hills, showing a similar theme about hiding in the book of Joshua.
Saul hid in a cave at En-Gedi, a parallel motif concerning kings and caves as hiding places.
Obadiah hid one hundred prophets in caves, illustrating caves as hiding places in biblical narratives.
